dissolved_oxygen.note: Oxygen Minimum Zone (OMZ) present at 100-200m depth

oxygen_minimum_zone.citation: Naqvi, S.W.A., et al. (2000). Increased marine productivity off Oman during the 1995 El Niño: Physical mechanisms and biological responses. Deep Sea Research Part II, 47(9-11), 2407-2410.

temperature.note: Arabian Sea surface warmer than Bay of Bengal

salinity.note: Higher salinity consistent with Arabian Sea; less monsoon runoff influence

dissolved_oxygen.note: Severe Oxygen Minimum Zone (OMZ) - one of world's most intense

chlorophyll_a.note: Lower productivity than Bay of Bengal; limited by low nutrients

oxygen_minimum_zone.implication: Severe hypoxia; one of world's most intense OMZs; benthic life severely limited
oxygen_minimum_zone.scientific_basis: Arabian Sea hosts one of Earth's most intense Oxygen Minimum Zones. Driven by strong stratification + limited ventilation. O2 <1 µmol/kg below 100m.
oxygen_minimum_zone.citation: Helly, B., & Levin, L. A. (2004). Global distribution of naturally occurring marine hypoxia on continental margins. Deep Sea Research Part I, 51(9), 1159-1168. DOI: 10.1016/j.dsr.2004.03.009

ocean_health_assessment.ecosystem_health: MODERATE-LOW - OMZ creates significant benthic habitat loss; pelagic fishery resilient
ocean_health_assessment.productivity: LOW - Limited by oxygen stress and nutrient availability
ocean_health_assessment.citation: CMFRI 2025 Marine Fish Landings Report; Oceanographic research on Arabian Sea oxygen dynamics

scoring_relevance.severity: EXTREME - One of world's most intense OMZs
scoring_relevance.traceability_support: ARGO oxygen profiles are critical for validating Arabian Sea catch authenticity
scoring_relevance.certification_value: ARGO data crucial for Arabian Sea exports; adds 5-8 points to score

temperature.note: Equatorial region with cooler SST due to upwelling

salinity.note: Fresh water from equatorial upwelling visible at surface

dissolved_oxygen.note: Better oxygenation than Arabian Sea due to upwelling; OMZ less severe

nitrate.note: High nutrient content from upwelling; supports high productivity

chlorophyll_a.note: Highest productivity of all three regions; strong subsurface maximum

oxygen_minimum_zone.implication: OMZ present but less severe than Arabian Sea; upwelling mitigates hypoxia
oxygen_minimum_zone.scientific_basis: Equatorial upwelling (3-8°N) brings nutrient-rich, oxygenated water to surface. Reduces severity of OMZ compared to Arabian Sea.
oxygen_minimum_zone.citation: Wyrtki, K. (1973). Physical oceanography of the Indian Ocean. The Biology of the Indian Ocean, 18-36. Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg.

ocean_health_assessment.productivity: HIGH - Equatorial upwelling creates one of world's most productive fishing grounds
